why: The printed working treats the string as fixed at BOTH ends (l = 3 lambda/2), contradicting its own stem, which says the string is fixed at one end with the vibrations imposed at the FREE end. A free end is an antinode, so the length is 3 complete loops PLUS a terminal quarter wavelength: l = 7 lambda/4, giving lambda = 0.60 m and v = 9.00 m/s. The book itself uses this treatment in Ex Q.19 - the same setup at 15 Hz - and prints the hint 'Remember that the free end is an antinode' there, so the two are inconsistent with each other and only Q.19 is right.
find:
\( \therefore l = 3\dfrac{\lambda}{2} \)
\( \therefore \lambda = \dfrac{2}{3} l = \dfrac{2}{3} \times 105 = 70\ \mathrm{cm} = 0.70 \) m
Speed of wave \( = \mathrm{v} = n\lambda \)
\( \mathrm{v} = 15 \times 0.70 = 10.50\ \mathrm{m\ s}^{-1} \)
replace:
The fixed end is a NODE and the free end, where the vibrations are imposed, is an ANTINODE. Each complete loop spans \( \dfrac{\lambda}{2} \), and the final stretch from the last node out to the free antinode adds a further \( \dfrac{\lambda}{4} \).
\( \therefore l = 3\dfrac{\lambda}{2} + \dfrac{\lambda}{4} = \dfrac{7\lambda}{4} \)
\( \therefore \lambda = \dfrac{4}{7} l = \dfrac{4}{7} \times 105 = 60\ \mathrm{cm} = 0.60 \) m
Speed of wave \( = \mathrm{v} = n\lambda \)
\( \mathrm{v} = 15 \times 0.60 = 9.00\ \mathrm{m\ s}^{-1} \)
